statement_record.book: A prop is a symmetric STRICT monoidal category (C, 0, +) whose set of objects is exactly ℕ, whose monoidal unit is the object 0 and whose monoidal product on objects is addition; hence every object n is the n-fold monoidal product of 1. The following prose lists the five data (i) hom-sets C(m,n), (ii) identities, (iii) symmetries σ_{m,n} : m+n -> n+m, (iv) composition, (v) monoidal product on morphisms, subject to the symmetric strict monoidal axioms.
statement_record.intree: Class PROP := { prop_cat : Category; prop_strict : StrictMonoidal; prop_symmetric : SymmetricMonoidal; prop_monoidal_coherence : strict_is_monoidal prop_strict = braided_is_monoidal (symmetric_is_braided prop_symmetric); prop_of_nat : nat -> obj prop_cat; prop_unit_zero : I = prop_of_nat 0; prop_tensor_plus : prop_of_nat m ⨂ prop_of_nat n = prop_of_nat (m+n) }
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: the object correspondence is a bare NAMING FUNCTION prop_of_nat : nat -> obj with propositional strictness equalities, and the class deliberately does not require it to be a bijection — the file's own header (Construction/PROP.v:60-66) states it 'does NOT assert the full "objects are exactly ℕ" condition'. All five data (i)-(v) are otherwise present (hom-setoids and composition from prop_cat, σ from prop_symmetric's braid, ⨂ on morphisms from the monoidal bifunctor), and strictness is Leibniz-level exactly as the book demands.

gap: Def 5.2 requires Ob(C) = ℕ; the in-tree class only requires a map nat -> obj with I = ⟦0⟧ and ⟦m⟧⨂⟦n⟧ = ⟦m+n⟧, admitting strict symmetric monoidal categories whose object monoid is merely GENERATED by ℕ (e.g. any such category with a chosen monoid map). statement_record.book: Given props C and D, a functor F : C -> D is a prop functor when (a) F is the identity on objects, F(n) = n for every n ∈ Ob(C) = Ob(D) = ℕ, and (b) F preserves the monoidal product of morphisms: F(f) + F(g) = F(f+g) for all f : m1 -> m2 and g : n1 -> n2.
statement_record.intree: Class StrictMonoidalFunctor { strict_functor_is_monoidal : MonoidalFunctor; strict_pure_obj : I = F I; strict_ap_obj : F x ⨂ F y = F (x ⨂ y); strict_pure_iso_id; strict_ap_iso_id } — plus, per construction, fobj := fun n : nat => n (RelabelFunctor, PresentedProj) or, in uniqueness statements, the hypothesis Hobj : ∀ n, G n = ⟦n⟧.
statement_record.strength_comparison: incomparable. intree-stronger: StrictMonoidalFunctor additionally requires unit preservation (strict_pure_obj/strict_pure_iso_id) and the full MonoidalFunctor coherence, and the library's actual PROP-morphism bundle also demands the braid square (SymmetricStrict, Construction/PROP/Universal.v:445, or BraidedMonoidalFunctor) — none of which Def 5.11 asks for, since a book prop functor need not preserve σ. intree-weaker: clause (a), identity-on-objects, is not a field of any class.
